title: Burst Assembly Under a Merge Tolerance and a Run-Length Floor

open_gate.condition: Cooper's visual review against the tape
open_gate.note: No numeric duration bar is pre-registered, deliberately -- D13 records that no burst timescale is established at usable precision. The scale judgment is Cooper's.

headline_metrics.name: prints_in_bursts_delta_floor_mp3
headline_metrics.interpretation: the floor DELETES -- objects and their prints leave the burst population

headline_metrics.name: prints_in_bursts_delta_merge_K5_d1
headline_metrics.interpretation: the merge PROMOTES -- short objects become longer ones, prints preserved; K=1 preserves them exactly by construction

headline_metrics.name: run_breaks_involving_ok_false_share
headline_metrics.interpretation: FIRST measurement of this split in the programme. Fragmentation is NOT a data-quality artifact -- 99.24% of breaks are real above-threshold gaps.

headline_metrics.name: counterfactual_declined_share_at_0.70
headline_metrics.interpretation: REPORTED, APPLIED NOWHERE. No cutoff enters the computation path.

headline_metrics.name: no_threshold_share_10c
headline_metrics.interpretation: 10c CANNOT decline on void magnitude (D13 threshold null, deliberate and permanent). A peak-count decline path exists in code and fired 0/504. insufficient_context (0.0%-66.7%) is a DATA-COVERAGE verdict, not comparable to v4's 10/100 shape verdict.

decisions_recorded.why: 10c applies NO run-length floor; 52.3% of its 170,722 objects are single-interval, so min_prints=3 deletes a majority inside the baseline. 2 is the structural no-op.

decisions_recorded.decision: D15 vs D20 for the decision number
decisions_recorded.why: Phase 11 already appended D15-D19; a second D15 would collide with a committed decision and append-only leaves no clean renumber. Text otherwise verbatim. OPEN FOR COOPER.

options_considered: reduced set on a reference variant
decisions_recorded.chose: full cross at all three kernels, cross-joined to all three variants
decisions_recorded.why: 10c has no reference variant (Amendment 3 A; selecting one is 10c escalation row 3), and extraction is a function of (event, kernel) only, so the variant axis is a cross-join. True cost 3x, not 9x. Widens the drafted allocation, narrows nothing.

decisions_recorded.chose: count, total and max duration; median reported un-gated
decisions_recorded.why: median object duration is NOT monotone under a correct merge -- [1s,1s,100s,100s] median 50.5s becomes [1s,1s,200s] median 1s. A10b.1-legitimate correction, made before any real event was read.

surprises: 10c applies no run-length floor at all -- 52.3% of its emitted sub-bursts (89,343 of 170,722) are single-interval, two-print objects, and its recorded 1.29 ms median is computed over that population.

Stage 1's recorded config_hash 998c2461 is STALE BY ONE COMMIT: commit 39ec87e edited config/phase_10c.json inside Stage 1, before 692d9d0 produced the T1 artifacts. True hash 17124203 (LF) / a0943e2a (raw CRLF). Carried in the digest, REPORT.md and s1_t0_denominator.json alike.

research/phase_10c/common.py::cfg_hash() hashes raw file bytes and is line-ending sensitive. Stage 0 recorded an LF-form hash, Stage 0b and Stage 1 CRLF-form. Not reproducible across clones with different core.autocrlf.

Only 0.761% of run breaks involve an ok=False interval -- fragmentation is essentially all real above-threshold gaps, so the separator axis this phase added is nearly inert (max 0.56% change in object count).

The floor/merge margin narrows sharply at the 2-minute kernel (1.39x vs 7.17x at 8 min): the shortest window produces the most ok=False intervals and the most fragmented runs, so there is more for a merge to join.
D15-D19 were already taken by Phase 11; CLAUDE.md's pointer list stops at D14 and is stale.
